# installation.mdx

Source: https://github.com/intentui/intentui/blob/3.x/src/content/docs/getting-started/installation.mdx

title: "Installation"
description: Install the necessary packages and set up your project. This tool automates the process, streamlining your setup and ensuring a smooth development experience.
order: 2

## Framework guides
You can choose from a list of frameworks to get started with Intent.
<FrameworkGuides/>

## Installation via CLI
Before executing the command, ensure that **tailwind** is installed. If not, follow the instructions [here](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/installation) for installation.

### Initial setup
Begin by executing this command:

<InstallCommand command="npx shadcn@latest init @intentui/theme-default"/>

If you see this output:

```
✖ Preflight checks.

A components.json file already exists at /Users/irsyad/code/acmes.
To start over, remove the components.json file and run init again
```

No problem: just run `npx shadcn@latest init @intentui/theme-default` again and it should complete successfully. See the related issue: [https://github.com/intentui/intentui/issues/518](https://github.com/intentui/intentui/issues/518).

Here are more theme options you can choose from:
```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/theme-blue
npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/theme-sky
npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/theme-indigo
npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/theme-emerald
npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/theme-teal
npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/theme-purple
npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/theme-pink
npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/theme-rose
npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/theme-green
npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/theme-lime
npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/theme-cyan
```

We use [shadcn CLI](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/cli) to manage the installation of Intent UI components.

<InstallCommand command="npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/combo-box"/>

Sometimes, you may want to add components individually, such as `select` and `text-field`. You can easily do this by using the following command:
<InstallCommand command="npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/select @intentui/text-field"/>

### Add all components
To add all components at once, use `@intentui/all`. This will install every available component in Intent UI in a single step.
<InstallCommand command="npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/all"/>

### Overwrite
You can override the existing components by using the `-o` flag. This will overwrite the existing files with the new ones.

<InstallCommand command="npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/text-field -o"/>

## Formatter
Intent UI utilizes the <NewTab href='https://biomejs.dev/'>Biome</NewTab> formatter for code formatting. To use the Biome formatter with Intent components, we recommend the following configuration:

<CodeBlock
  source={{
      'biome.json': 'installation/biome.json',
  }} />

## Manual installation
To begin setting up the design system, start by installing these packages:

<InstallCommand command="npm i react-aria-components tailwindcss-react-aria-components"/>

Next, add **Tailwind Variant**, **Tailwind Merge**, and for utility functions:

<InstallCommand command="npm i tailwind-variants tailwind-merge"/>

Following that, include the **Tailwind Animate** for managing animations and **Intent Icons** for icons:

<InstallCommand command="npm i @heroicons/react tw-animate-css"/>

### Style and primitive
After installing the required packages, you can copy the CSS below into your global CSS file and move the primitives to your UI folder. Primitives serve as utilities for managing states, including `focusRing`, `focusStyles`, and `focusButtonStyles`.

<CodeBlock
    source={{
        'app/globals.css': 'installation/main.css',
        'lib/primitive.ts': 'installation/primitive.ts',
    }} />

### Hooks

Hooks are only used in specific components like the **Navbar**, **Sidebar**, **Popover**, and **Command Menu**. If you're using the **Intent CLI**, it will handle this automatically; otherwise, download the file below.

<CodeBlock
    source={{
        'hooks/use-media-query.ts': 'hooks/use-media-query.ts',
    }} />

### Fonts
This is currently using the [Inter font](https://rsms.me/inter/). If you want to use a different font, you can define your font-family in your JS or CSS file.

### Stylesheet
When you're working with a stylesheet, you can define your `@font-face` in your css file.

```
@font-face {
  font-family: 'Inter';
  font-style: normal;
  font-weight: 100 900;
  font-display: swap;
  src: url("InterVariable.woff2") format("woff2");
}
```

### Next.js
If you're using Next.js, you don't even need CSS files. Just define your font in your layout file.

```
import localFont from 'next/font/local'

const fontSans = localFont({
  src: [{path: './fonts/Inter.woff2'}],
  variable: '--font-sans'
})
```

Then, apply the `fontSans` to the `body` tag like this:

```tsx
<body
  className={`font-sans antialiased ${fontSans.variable}`}
/>
```

Then, you can use the variable in your main css file like this:

```css
@theme {
  --font-sans: var(--font-inter-sans), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif, "Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji",
  "Segoe UI Symbol", "Noto Color Emoji";
  --font-mono: var(--font-geist-mono), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif, "Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji",
  "Segoe UI Symbol", "Noto Color Emoji";

  // Your other variables
}
```

For more information, refer to the [Tailwind documentation](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/font-family#customizing-the-default-font) and [Next.js documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/optimizing/fonts).

## IntelliSense
If you want your development environment to be more intelligent, you can follow instructions here at [Tailwind Variants](https://www.tailwind-variants.org/docs/getting-started#intellisense-setup-optional).

# introduction.mdx

Source: https://github.com/intentui/intentui/blob/3.x/src/content/docs/getting-started/introduction.mdx

title: "Introduction"
description: "Take a practical tour of this open source design system built on React Aria, with useful tips to quickly fix missing props and common integration issues."
order: 1

## Introduction
Intent UI is more than just a design system. It is a comprehensive toolkit designed to make creating accessible, visually stunning, and highly customizable user interfaces effortless. Built on top of **React Aria Components**, Intent leverages their accessibility-first approach to ensure your designs are inclusive and meet modern accessibility standards, allowing you to focus on delivering exceptional user experiences.

**Why choose Intent UI?** It includes **Tailwind CSS** for seamless, modern styling, a beautifully crafted icon library to enhance your designs, and a robust color system offering four formats and **shades from 50 to 950**. This flexibility ensures your designs are consistent, scalable, and visually appealing.

## Shoutout
A huge thank you to [Devon Govett](https://x.com/devongovett) and the React Aria team for their outstanding work on the [React Aria Components](https://react-aria.adobe.com/?utm_source=intentui.com&utm_medium=docs&utm_campaign=referral). Their dedication has set a new benchmark for excellence! I also want to extend my gratitude to [Adam Wathan](https://x.com/adamwathan) and his team for creating the incredible Tailwind CSS. This project wouldn’t be possible without it.

## What's the scoop on React Aria?

React Aria offers a collection of foundational React components and hooks designed to facilitate the creation of accessible, high-quality UI components effortlessly.

It includes key features like accessibility, internationalization, smooth interactions, and intelligent behavior, allowing you to focus on designing your unique aesthetic. Tested across various devices and assistive technologies, React Aria ensures a seamless user experience for everyone.

## Why React Aria?

React Aria is an excellent starting point for developing accessible React components and provides a great opportunity to learn how to build your own. It is especially beneficial for testing your components in real-world scenarios, which is crucial for deploying them in production environments.

## Tailwind CSS
All components are built with Tailwind CSS v4, which provides a robust set of utility classes for styling. This allows you to quickly and easily customize the appearance of your components without having to write custom CSS.

## Blocks
Want to move fast without spending hours building components? No problem! **[Intent UI Design](https://dub.sh/designiui)** offers a collection of ready-to-use components, covering everything from **Application** and **Marketing** to **Charts** and **Commerce**. Easily customize them to fit your needs and build faster than ever.

## FAQ
This is a list of frequently asked questions about Intent UI.

* Is it free and open source? **Yes.**
* Is it a design system? **Yes.**
* Is it a component library? **No. Just copy and paste.**
* Can I use it outside of React? **No.**
* What frameworks are supported? **Anything that supports React.**
* Can I use it with TypeScript? **Yes, in fact, it is written in TypeScript.**
* Can I use it in my project? **Yes, you can use it for both personal and commercial projects without needing to provide attribution. However, I’d love to see what you build, so if you’re up for it, [let me know](https://x.com/irsyad)** 🙂

---

# vite.mdx

Source: https://github.com/intentui/intentui/blob/3.x/src/content/docs/getting-started/vite.mdx

title: "Vite"
description: Set up Intent in your Vite project with React and Tailwind CSS using a quick and efficient installation process, following step-by-step guide for seamless integration.

## Installation
Start a new project with the following command:
<InstallCommand command="npm create vite@latest"/>

Next, install Tailwind CSS along with the Tailwind CSS Vite plugin:
<InstallCommand command="npm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite"/>

## Vite.config.ts
Now, open your `vite.config.ts` file and add the following to the `plugins` array:
```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite'

// https://vite.dev/config/
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    tailwindcss(),
    react()
  ],
})
```

## Tsconfig.json
To ensure proper path resolution, update your `tsconfig.json` file with the following paths:
```json
{
  "files": [],
  "references": [
    {
      "path": "./tsconfig.app.json"
    },
    {
      "path": "./tsconfig.node.json"
    }
  ],
  "compilerOptions": {
    "baseUrl": ".",
    "paths": {
      "@/*": ["./src/*"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Install Intent UI
After you set up all the necessary configurations, you can install Intent UI by running the following command:
<InstallCommand command="npx shadcn@latest init @intentui/theme-default"/>

## Adding components
Add Intent UI components to your project with the following command:
<InstallCommand command="npx shadcn@latest add @intentui/text-field @intentui/button @intentui/menu"/>

## Other framework
You might be interested in using Intent with other frameworks.

# contribution-guide.mdx

Source: https://github.com/intentui/intentui/blob/3.x/src/content/docs/prologue/contribution-guide.mdx

title: "Contribution Guide"
description: Over 50 accessible components, neatly organized into sections, ensuring usability and ease of access for everyone. Perfect for a range of applications and users.
order: 3

## Contribution guide

Thanks for jumping in to contribute at intentui.com. We’re thrilled to have you on board!

Quick ask: take a moment to review this doc before submitting your first pull request. Also, check out the open issues and pull requests to avoid doubling up on any efforts.

## Getting started

1. Fork the repository.
2. Clone the forked repository.
3. Install the dependencies with `npm run first-time`.
4. Create a new branch: `git checkout -b features`.
5. Make your changes.
6. And add all: `git add .`
7. Push and submit a pull request.

## How to contribute

### Reporting bugs

Before creating bug reports, please check the existing issues as you might find out that you don't need to create one. When you are creating a bug report, please include as many details as possible.

### Suggesting enhancements

Enhancement suggestions are tracked as GitHub issues. When you are creating an enhancement suggestion, please include as many details as possible.

### Pull requests

Please follow these guidelines when submitting pull requests:

1. Fork the repository and create your branch from `main`.
2. Run `npm run lint` to check your code for linting errors.
3. If you've added code that should be tested, add tests.
4. Format your code with `npm run format`.
5. Ensure everything is working as expected by running `npm run r` which will build the registry and generate the sidebar.
6. Make sure your code lints.
7. Make sure your commit messages are clear.

## Folder structure

The folder structure is essential for grasping the codebase and understanding the underlying workflow.

### Components
The `components` folder forms the backbone of the project, housing the `ui`, `docs`, and `blocks` directories.
```
components
├── blocks
├── code
├── docs
│   ├── anatomies
│   ├── buttons ...
│   ├── charts ...
│   ├── collections ...
│   ├── colors ...
│   ├── controls ...
│   ├── date-and-time ...
│   ├── drag-and-drop ...
│   ├── forms ...
│   ├── media ...
│   ├── navigation ...
│   ├── outside ...
│   ├── overlays ...
│   ├── pickers ...
│   ├── statuses ...
│   └── surfaces ...
├── experimental
└── ui
```
The core ui is inside `components/ui`, and the demo you see on the docs is inside `components/examples`.

### Registry
The registry is a file that contains all the components and their files. It is used to generate the `demo`, `ui`, `blocks` and `anatomies` on the docs.
```
public/registry
├── anatomies
├── blocks
│   ├── navbar ...
│   └── sidebar ...
├── demo
│   ├── buttons ...
│   ├── charts ...
│   ├── collections ...
│   ├── colors ...
│   ├── controls ...
│   ├── date-and-time ...
│   ├── drag-and-drop
│   ├── forms ...
│   ├── media
│   ├── navigation ...
│   ├── outside
│   ├── overlays ...
│   ├── pickers ...
│   ├── statuses ...
│   └── surfaces ...
├── docs
│   └── installation
└── ui
```

All of this is generated by the `resources/scripts/build-registry.ts` script by running `npm run b`.

## Code of conduct

The Intent UI code of conduct is inspired by the Laravel and Ruby code of conduct. Any violations of this code may be reported to [Irsyad](https://x.com/irsyad):

- Participants will respect and be tolerant of differing views and opinions.
- Participants must ensure that their language and actions remain professional and free of personal attacks or disparaging remarks.
- When interpreting the words and actions of others, participants should always assume good intentions.
- Behavior that can reasonably be considered harassment or discrimination will not be tolerated.

## License

By contributing to Intent UI, you agree that your contributions will be licensed under its MIT license.

# upgrade-guide.mdx

Source: https://github.com/intentui/intentui/blob/3.x/src/content/docs/prologue/upgrade-guide.mdx

title: "Upgrade Guide"
description: "This guide walks you through a seamless upgrade from Intent UI v2 to Intent UI v3, covering key changes, migration steps, and common pitfalls to avoid."
order: 2

## 2026 Upgrade Guide
There's nothing to upgrade for 2026. Enjoy using Intent UI! If you're looking for the latest features, check out the [2026 Release Notes](/docs/prologue/release-notes).

## 2025 Upgrade Guide
Not sure what's new or what has changed? Don’t worry! You can find all the updates in [Release v3](/blog/release-v3).

## Upgrade steps
- Change any of `square-petite`, `extra-small`, `small`, `medium`, `large` to `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, and `sq-[xs, sm, md, lg]` in the `size` prop.
- Remove the `shape` prop from `Button`, `Badge`, `Tag`, and `Toggle`. Use the `isCircle` prop instead.
- Remove `focusRing` and `focusStyles` from `primitive.ts`—they are no longer used.

---
